title: DataClaw0: Data Refinement as a Learnable Skill
hook: Instead of scrubbing data with fixed rules, what if an agent learned to tailor it? DataClaw0 turns data refinement into a trainable skill judged by how well models train on its output.
key_points: Reframes data processing as a learnable capability — 'agentic data tailoring' — not fixed heuristics or generic VLM annotation.
A two-stage pipeline grounds generative synthesis in deterministic 'Factual Anchors' to build training data across five domains.
The DataClaw_0-9B model combines supervised fine-tuning with GRPO to align to complex refinement intents.
DataClaw_0-val is introduced as the first benchmark dedicated to data refinement.
Validation is downstream post-training: tailored data improved video generation, real-world VQA, and GUI navigation under limited data.
content_html: Raw multimodal streams are high-entropy: noisy, unstructured, and hard to turn into good training data. The usual fixes — heuristic rules or general vision-language models doing passive annotation — are costly and miss the deeper procedural logic in the data. Wan, Ma, Gong and colleagues propose elevating data processing itself to a learnable capability they call agentic data tailoring.
extra_html:
How it works

The idea is to actively refine and structure data to align with diverse user and downstream intents, rather than apply one fixed cleaning recipe. To get training data for such a high-order skill, the authors design a two-stage pipeline that grounds generative semantic synthesis in deterministic "Factual Anchors," yielding a large dataset across five physical and digital domains. The DataClaw_0-9B model is then trained with supervised fine-tuning plus Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to align with complex tailoring intents, and DataClaw_0-val is introduced as the first benchmark dedicated to data refinement.

Why it matters

Crucially, the work judges tailored data by the only test that matters in practice: downstream post-training. Models trained on DataClaw0's output improved on video generation, real-world VQA, and GUI navigation under limited-data regimes — evidence that treating data curation as a learnable, intent-aware skill can beat static heuristics.

related.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes LMs Better
related.hook: Training corpora are full of copies — one 61-word sentence shows up 60,000+ times in C4. Strip the duplicates and models memorize far less and evaluate more honestly.

related.title: The Pile: 800GB of Diverse Text
related.hook: Web text alone leaves gaps. The Pile stitches together 22 curated sources — academic and professional — so a language model picks up knowledge plain web crawls miss.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'agentic data tailoring' replace, and how?
flashcards.back_html: It replaces fixed heuristic rules and generic VLM annotation with a learnable agent that actively refines and structures raw data to fit specific downstream intents.

flashcards.prompt: How does DataClaw0 ultimately validate the data it produces?

choices.text: By downstream post-training — checking whether models trained on the tailored data improve on tasks like VQA and GUI navigation
By human ratings of data cleanliness alone
By counting how many examples it removes

flashcards.explanation_html: The authors adopt downstream post-training as the 'ultimate validation touchstone', measuring the tailored data by the performance of models trained on it.

flashcards.prompt: What role do 'Factual Anchors' play in DataClaw0's pipeline?
flashcards.back_html: They are deterministic grounding points for the generative semantic synthesis, keeping the synthesized dataset tied to facts rather than free-floating hallucination.
